input.quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created and paid for by us, with only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables). The perpetual licence in 13.2, referenced by 14.3, reaches only Vendor Technology delivered paid-up or embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverables themselves, so it does not cure the gap; the revocable/term-limited licence also sits awkwardly with 10.1 (rights in accepted Deliverables continue) and 6.2/10.2 (we pay for Deliverables). Customer Data ownership (14.1), Vendor Technology retention (14.3) and the no-joint-ownership rule (14.4) are all satisfactory. Redline reverses the assignment while expressly preserving Vendor's background IP and the embedded-IP licence.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable upon its creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3, and the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies to any Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we commission, so we have reversed the assignment in 14.2 and confirmed Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology with the Section 13.2 perpetual licence to anything embedded in a Deliverable. A revocable, term-limited licence to Deliverables we pay for is not workable for us; if Vendor cannot assign, our fallback is Vendor ownership with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for us to use, modify, and sublicense the Deliverables for our business.
proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; preserve Vendor Technology retention and embedded-IP licence.
